config.title: Who Owed Due Care?
config.sub: Seventeen real security failures across the eight CISSP domains, replayed so you make the calls. Every case ends at the same question: where should the control have been, and who was placed to apply it?
config.footer: Example extract from the CISSP casebook built with the Trust Course Kit. Every real fact has a source in its lesson.
questions: Who owns this, and who answers for it?
Did we do the research before we took it on?
Does anyone hold more access than the job needs?
Can one person do this alone?
Is it locked by default, and does it fail closed?
If this layer fails, what stands behind it?
Even when we trust it, who verifies?
Whose control is this: ours or the provider's?

questionHints: Fails when nobody was named or accountable for the system, the data or the decision.
Fails when risks were not investigated before taking on a company, a vendor or a platform.
Fails when an account, role or permission existed beyond what the job needed.
Fails when one person could make a critical change with no second person involved.
Fails when the default setting, or the state after a failure, was open instead of closed.
Fails when there was only one layer, and nothing behind it when it gave way.
Fails when something trusted (a person, an update, an alert, a test, a deployment) was not checked.
Fails when each side assumed the other was responsible for a control.
